statements.text: Right now there is virtually no regulation of AI at the federal level. I want America to develop and to deploy this technology in a way that is transparent and safe. We've got to make sure the benefits of AI are there for everyone, not just billionaires and technology experts... I had the chance last week to speak to the godfather of AI, Geoffrey Hinton. It was a really amazing conversation, and I have to say, I learned a lot. But what I learned from him is that there are a lot of risks. We need to be aware of them, and we need to deal with them. Is AI safe for our kids? Is it safe for someone with a mental health issue? Does it inflame delusions? There are risks from bad actors, whether it's a cyberattack or whether it's a deepfake scam.
statements.venue: Remarks at Transparency Coalition event, as reported by Transparency Coalition

statements.text: I'm not an expert in AI, I'm a former preschool teacher. But I'll tell you what: I ran for office exactly because I believe regular people deserve a say in how their government is run—the exact same is true for the development of this technology. There are real opportunities with AI—in medicine, in discovery. But this technology will also likely mean disruption and it poses real challenges and threats. And right now regulation of AI is virtually nonexistent at the federal level.

I recently spoke with the so-called godfather of AI, Geoffrey Hinton, he made it absolutely clear that there are real safety risks that require urgent action. When the stakes are this high, we cannot take safety for granted. That's just common sense. No one would say nuclear plants can regulate themselves—or drug companies. Why would we ignore something as powerful and potentially dangerous as AI?

Trump wants to call AI risks a 'hoax' and call it a day. His most significant AI policies to date? He tried to rename it, and threatened states' funding if they dare to regulate it. Trump shaking hands with billionaires and saying they can regulate themselves is not going to cut it. We can't afford to regulate AI with nothing but a pinky promise. We cannot just wait for the worst risks of this technology to become reality before we take action.

The need for federal guardrails around AI is absolutely urgent. 

AI should be safe, transparent, and actually benefit working people–not just billionaires.

I was in Olympia to hear what WA leaders are already doing to regulate AI. https://t.co/azgFzloJM0

Everyone’s talking about AI. In Pullman, we mean Apple Innovation. 🍎
